items.subject: CHOSEN BRICK Iranian-state cyber targeting and leak-site propagation

observations.source: UK National Cyber Security Centre with FBI and Netherlands AIVD
observations.statement_identity: The joint advisory says CHOSEN BRICK malware has been used by Iranian state cyber actors to target dissidents, activists and journalists and can collect contacts, emails and social-media messages.
NCSC said personal details of some previous victims later appeared on pro-Iranian leak sites. The advisory does not identify every leak-site operator or equate those sites with Handala.

public_receipts.attribution: UK NCSC / U.S. FBI / Netherlands AIVD
UK NCSC with allied technical reporting

items.attribution_scope: The advisory attributes CHOSEN BRICK activity to Iranian state cyber actors. It does not identify Handala as the malware operator, prove a common operator for every pro-Iranian leak site, or establish that every later leak-site publication originated from CHOSEN BRICK collection.
items.downstream_note: Treat malware compromise, victim-data collection, leak-site publication, and narrative amplification as separate graph events. Do not merge this discovery with Handala solely because both involve Iranian state-linked cyber activity and public leak sites.
items.review_reason: This is a current public information-operation/cyber-propagation discovery with no canonical Lie Ledger family. Claims Forensics should decide whether any specific public assertion or leak-derived narrative warrants a claim family before Web of Lies scores propagation or source behavior.

items.subject: Ethan Levins assertion that all damage in Israel that day came from two missiles and that Iran had thousands more

observations.source: Ethan Levins as quoted by Press TV and secondary Telegram preservation
observations.statement_identity: The quoted statement said all the damage that day in Israel was caused by two missiles.

observations.source: Ethan Levins as quoted by Press TV and secondary Telegram preservation
observations.statement_identity: The quoted statement added that Iran had thousands more missiles.

items.attribution_scope: Two independent public Telegram preservations reproduce the same attributed wording. The original Ethan Levins post URL was not recovered in this tranche, so the discovery preserves quotation provenance rather than claiming an original-post receipt.
items.downstream_note: Claims Forensics should atomize the damage-causation claim separately from the missile-stockpile claim. WOL must not treat Press TV's quotation as independent corroboration of either proposition, nor infer control/agency from Press TV reuse.
items.review_reason: No current canonical family cleanly adjudicates the combined March 22 proposition about all same-day Israeli damage coming from two missiles plus a remaining Iranian stockpile in the thousands.

content_body_evidence.capture_scope: The complete quoted passage preserved by Press TV and a second public Telegram relay is available for the two propositions recorded here. The original Ethan post URL was not recovered, so analysis is limited to the preserved quotation.

body_claims.statement_identity: All of the cited same-day damage in Israel was attributed to two missiles.
body_claims.speaker: Ethan Levins
body_claims.evidence_scope: Quoted passage preserved by two public Telegram surfaces.

body_claims.statement_identity: Iran was said to retain thousands more missiles.
body_claims.speaker: Ethan Levins
body_claims.evidence_scope: Quoted passage preserved by two public Telegram surfaces.

factual_substrate.statement: The quoted passage points to visible same-day damage in Israel as the observable substrate.
factual_substrate.evidence_note: Physical damage that day is independently observable; the decomposition does not treat the quote as proof of exact causation.

inferential_bridges.statement: The passage attributes all referenced same-day damage to only two missiles.
inferential_bridges.evidentiary_issue: Observed damage does not by itself establish that exactly two missiles caused all of it; site-by-site strike attribution is required.
competing_explanations: More than two impactors contributed to the observed damage.
The quoted passage selected a subset of damage while presenting it as the whole.
Damage attribution may mix direct missile effects with secondary effects.

inferential_bridges.statement: The visible damage is used rhetorically to imply a much larger remaining strike capacity because Iran allegedly has thousands more missiles.
inferential_bridges.evidentiary_issue: Even if the damage attribution were correct, it does not establish the size, readiness, survivability or composition of Iran's remaining missile inventory.
competing_explanations: Headline stockpile figures may include missiles unsuitable for the same target/effect.
Inventory estimates may not reflect launchers, readiness, survivability or expendable operational stock.

conclusions.statement: The passage implies that the observed damage demonstrates a substantially larger latent Iranian ability to reproduce or scale those effects.

analysis_decomposition.decomposition_note: The visible-damage substrate and the causal/stockpile inference are separate propositions. A true observation about damage cannot validate either the exact two-missile attribution or the extrapolation to future strike capacity.

items.subject: Handala Hack public cyber / psychological-operations infrastructure attributed by U.S. authorities to Iran's MOIS

observations.statement_identity: DOJ said four seized domains, including Handala-hack.to and Handala-redwanted.to, were used by Iran's Ministry of Intelligence and Security for hacking-linked psychological operations, public hack claims, stolen-data publication, threats and transnational repression.

observations.source: Handala Hack claim preserved in DOJ seizure materials
observations.statement_identity: Handala Hack claimed a destructive malware attack against a U.S.-based multinational medical technologies firm. This is preserved as a claimed operation; the public claim does not by itself establish the technical facts of the compromise.

observations.source: Handala Hack claims preserved in DOJ seizure materials
observations.statement_identity: DOJ documented Handala public posts claiming theft of data and publishing personal or confidential information. The seizure record establishes the messaging infrastructure and attributed operator relationship; authenticity of every released item remains a separate evidentiary question.

public_receipts.attribution: U.S. Department of Justice / FBI investigation and seizure affidavit

items.attribution_scope: The public U.S. record supports attribution of the seized Handala domains and associated psychological-operations infrastructure to MOIS. It does not independently verify every hack claim published by the persona, authenticate every leaked file, or identify every individual operator behind each post.
items.downstream_note: If Claims Forensics creates a canonical claim family for a specific Handala wartime hack/leak assertion, preserve the distinction between the public claim, independently verified compromise, released-material authenticity, and downstream repetition. Do not treat the DOJ infrastructure attribution as automatic verification of every claimed operation.
items.review_reason: This is a public-source information-operation actor discovery with strong organizational attribution but no current canonical Lie Ledger family. It belongs outside lineage/Hall scoring until Claims Forensics assigns a claim family or determines that no public claim adjudication is warranted.

items.subject: Lim Tean causal inference that renewed U.S. strikes were producing the opposite of reopening Hormuz

observations.statement_identity: The article accurately cited sharply reduced vessel transits and then argued that the sequence 'more bombs, fewer ships' showed U.S. strikes were themselves producing the shutdown rather than reopening the strait.

public_receipts.attribution: S&P Global Commodities at Sea / Platts

content_body_evidence.capture_scope: The full published commentary is publicly readable, allowing separation of the transit-count substrate from the causal bridge and conclusion.

body_claims.statement_identity: Hormuz vessel traffic was far below the prewar baseline, including 11 transits on July 12 and only a few commodity-vessel crossings later in the week.
body_claims.speaker: Lim Tean
body_claims.evidence_scope: Full-text commentary plus independent maritime reporting.

body_claims.statement_identity: The article concludes that successive U.S. strike waves were producing the opposite of their stated navigation objective and deepening the shutdown.
body_claims.speaker: Lim Tean

factual_substrate.statement: Hormuz traffic fell drastically from roughly 125-130 daily prewar transits; independent reporting also recorded 11 ships on July 12 and very low subsequent traffic.
factual_substrate.evidence_note: Independent S&P Global and Reuters reporting supports the broad traffic-collapse substrate while also warning that AIS-dark traffic makes raw visible counts incomplete.

inferential_bridges.statement: Temporal correlation between renewed U.S. strike waves and lower visible ship counts is treated as evidence that the U.S. strikes themselves were producing the shutdown.
inferential_bridges.evidentiary_issue: The sequence alone does not isolate U.S. strikes as the cause. Contemporary reporting also identifies renewed Iranian attacks on commercial vessels, blockade effects, insurer/crew risk, and AIS-dark transits as material contributors.
competing_explanations: Renewed Iranian attacks on commercial vessels directly increased perceived transit risk.
The U.S. blockade and wider U.S.-Iran escalation jointly depressed commercial confidence.
Insurer, charterer and crew risk decisions reduced traffic independently of any single strike wave.
AIS-dark traffic means visible transits undercount some actual movement.

conclusions.statement: The article concludes that U.S. military escalation was measurably producing the opposite of reopening Hormuz.

analysis_decomposition.decomposition_note: The traffic-collapse numbers can be substantially correct while the claimed causal explanation remains unresolved or misleading. WOL therefore preserves the supported substrate and routes the causal bridge separately for Claims Forensics review.

items.attribution_scope: The full commentary supports attribution of the causal argument to Lim Tean. Independent maritime reporting supports the broad traffic decline but also supplies competing causes and measurement limits.
items.downstream_note: Claims Forensics should adjudicate the causal bridge, not merely the vessel counts. Do not mark the analysis sound solely because the underlying transit figures are accurate.
items.review_reason: The current Hormuz control family addresses competing control framing, but this article adds a distinct causal proposition: that U.S. strikes themselves were producing the shipping shutdown. The supported substrate and causal conclusion must be adjudicated separately.

items.subject: MeidasTouch broad assertion that Iran was easily destroying multiple U.S. military bases in the Middle East

observations.statement_identity: The MeidasTouch episode title said Iran 'INSTANTLY DESTROYS US BASES' and the publisher description said Iran was 'easily destroying multiple United States military bases in the Middle East.'

items.attribution_scope: The public YouTube publication supports that MeidasTouch used the broad destruction wording. This discovery does not decide which specific bases or subfacilities the episode discussed, whether the body qualified the headline, or the final truth disposition.
items.downstream_note: Claims Forensics should atomize the broad plural-base destruction proposition against the facility/BDA record before Web of Lies assigns any falsehood, mutation, or behavioral finding. Do not collapse real severe subfacility damage into whole-base destruction or vice versa.
items.review_reason: Current canonical families adjudicate named facilities and several specific BDA exaggerations, but no clean single canonical claim atom was found for this publisher's broad July 12 proposition that multiple U.S. military bases were destroyed.

items.subject: Valenti Videos headline asserting Iran mobilized 31 million soldiers for a U.S. invasion

observations.statement_identity: The public Valenti Videos channel listed a video titled 'Iran mobilizes 31 MILLION soldiers for the U.S invasion.'

items.attribution_scope: The public channel index preserves the headline assertion. It does not establish whether the body later qualified '31 million' as registrations in a broader Janfada campaign, military/security volunteers, projected participants, or literal trained soldiers.
items.downstream_note: Compare against the canonical Sep. 18 training family, which currently treats >600,000 registrations as unresolved and >1 million participants as a prospective projection. Claims Forensics should determine whether the 31-million-soldiers wording is a materially new proposition or a qualifier-stripping mutation before WOL scores it.
items.review_reason: The existing canonical military-training family does not currently contain a 31-million-soldier proposition. WOL must not silently substitute the title for the >600,000 / >1 million canonical atoms.

content_body_evidence.capture_scope: Publisher title/description/video identity captured. Spoken-body transcript or timestamped direct review is not yet preserved, so no narrative/inference decomposition is permitted.

items.subject: Valenti Videos headline asserting leaked U.S. photos show Middle East bases completely destroyed

observations.statement_identity: The public Valenti Videos channel listed a video titled 'U.S Soldiers LEAK PHOTOS of our bases in the Middle East; THEY'RE COMPLETELY DESTROYED!'

items.attribution_scope: The title supports a broad whole-base destruction assertion but does not identify the facilities, photos, dates, or whether the body narrows the claim to specific damaged subfacilities.
items.downstream_note: Claims Forensics should identify the referenced facilities and atomize physical damage versus whole-base operational destruction. Real severe U.S. base damage is independently established in the war record; that fact neither proves nor disproves this broader title without facility-level matching.
items.review_reason: The title does not cleanly map to one current canonical BDA family. It may span Al Udeid, Bahrain, Erbil, Jordan or other facilities and requires proposition-level assignment before Web of Lies behavior scoring.

content_body_evidence.capture_scope: Publisher title/description/video identity captured. Spoken-body transcript or timestamped direct review is not yet preserved, so no narrative/inference decomposition is permitted.

items.subject: Valenti Videos allegation that the U.S. government was covering up a massive number of U.S. casualties

observations.statement_identity: The publisher titled a July 21 episode 'The U.S Government is COVERING UP the MASSIVE amount of U.S Casualties.'

items.attribution_scope: The receipts establish a publisher-authored concealment allegation. They do not establish what casualty number the body asserted, what evidence was offered for concealment, or whether the episode distinguished killed, wounded, evacuated, contractor, diplomatic, and allied casualties.
items.downstream_note: Claims Forensics should treat this as a concealment proposition distinct from CHAIN-CL-200-US-DEAD. A false or inflated casualty count and a claim that the government knowingly concealed casualties are separate atomic propositions with different evidence and knowledge requirements.
items.review_reason: No current canonical family cleanly adjudicates the July 21 concealment allegation itself. The existing 200-dead family concerns an IRGC casualty-count assertion, not whether U.S. authorities concealed a larger casualty total.

content_body_evidence.capture_scope: Publisher title/description/video identity captured. Spoken-body transcript or timestamped direct review is not yet preserved, so no narrative/inference decomposition is permitted.

items.subject: Valenti Videos allegation that the U.S. military allowed Iranian missiles to hit U.S. bases

observations.statement_identity: The publisher listed an episode titled 'U.S Military ALLOWS IRANIAN MISSILES to hit our bases. Ukraine joins the Iran War.'

items.attribution_scope: The publisher title establishes that Valenti said the U.S. military 'allows' Iranian missiles to hit bases. Subsequent evidence review shows the literal proposition that commanders sometimes deliberately declined interception of low-value trajectories is not inherently unsupported. The distinct body-level motive claim reported by project-owner direct review—that the U.S. did not care / permissively let strikes occur to provoke anger or political reaction—requires transcript/timestamp preservation before WOL scores it.
items.downstream_note: Do not score the title alone as bullshit. Separate (1) documented interceptor rationing/threat-based non-interception from (2) the stronger alleged motive/permission theory in the spoken body. The latter remains a transcript-capture target.
items.review_reason: The title overlaps a supportable operational practice, while the reported body motive proposition is materially stronger and must be preserved from the spoken content before source-behavior scoring.

content_body_evidence.capture_scope: Publisher title/description/video identity captured. Spoken-body transcript or timestamped direct review is not yet preserved, so no narrative/inference decomposition is permitted.

project_owner_direct_review.observation: Project owner reports Valenti said the U.S. essentially did not care and permitted the strikes in order to anger other actors, not merely that defenses rationed interceptors against missiles expected to miss valuable targets.
project_owner_direct_review.evidentiary_limit: Exact captions/timestamps are not yet machine-recovered, so this body-level motive proposition is not yet a scored WOL-native incident.
